answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards at random, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; turns proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup: “randomly select number of players + 1” Factory cards; one token on each of the “11 marked territories”; choose one structure bonus tile; “The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: Each player starts their character at their home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining that base; four mechs over the abilities on their Faction Mat; six stars by their faction emblem; six technology cubes in the Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits on its bottom-row circular spaces; the remaining six workers on its Produce red rectangles; and their action token beside the Player Mat. Leave faction one-time recruit spaces empty. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. The Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup piece table and steps 3–4: “Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw”; “Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives (two objective cards).”

answers.answer: You must move the action token to a different section, but may take neither action, either one, or both; if taking both, take top before bottom. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. You may use top-row gains to pay a bottom-row cost. Costs are all exposed red boxes before the action and must be paid in full first; benefits are exposed green boxes and may be taken as much or as little as desired. Exact bottom-row costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “different section from last turn”; “top action once, then ... bottom action once”; “bottom first is not allowed”; full cost before choosing “as much or as little” green-box benefit.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and all its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay resource costs from any territories you currently control, even when taking the action elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: “An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources”; “Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities”; pay from “any territories you currently control.”

answers.answer: No. On the default Move, choose up to two different units and move each one adjacent territory; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice. All units can carry any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker's transport does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself (or move onto a mech before that mech moves).
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: “move up to two different units, one adjacent territory each”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; worker transport does not count as its own movement.

answers.answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn; the workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. The mover loses one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero or insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs, and a worker cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy workers. The summary does not specifically state whether a worker may independently enter territory controlled only by enemy characters/mechs in every possible case beyond its general rule: a worker cannot independently move into or out of such territory.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers “immediately retreat to their home base”; “Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero”; workers cannot independently move “into or out of” territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

answers.answer: After all units finish a Move action, resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; if multiple combats occur, the attacker chooses their order. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats “before the bottom-row action”; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Workers cannot independently move “into or out of” enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster: “Pay $1”; Trade: “Pay $1”; resource placement requires a controlled territory with a worker; empty combat deck is replenished from discards, and if both are empty draw none.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Revealing new costs by taking workers affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps: pay every exposed cost “in full before production”; choose up to two territories; each worker produces; take new workers “left to right”; new costs affect “future Produce actions.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade — oil and exposed mat cost; Deploy — metal and controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; ability applies to character and every mech. Completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. An enemy unit on the territory does not give it your structure's ability. You retain the ability without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. A controlled Mill gives an extra Produce territory; it counts as one producing worker, and actual workers there also each produce normally. Your Mine is a personal tunnel usable for your unit movement even while its territory is enemy-controlled, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions. Opponents cannot use your building abilities.
answers.evidence: Build: controlled territory with your worker; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden; structures “cannot be moved or destroyed.” Mill works “only while controlled”; Mine is a personal tunnel “even when enemy-controlled.”

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. For the rest of the game, when you, your immediate left neighbor, or immediate right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, you may gain its exposed circle bonus. Resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game, the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist: recruit from “any bottom-row section,” place on any open Faction Mat one-time bonus; ongoing bonus is where removed. Ongoing recruits: active, left, right; two-player opponent triggers once.

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly and simultaneously chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of 7 and their current power. They may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if at least one worker is present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial power and card values; attacker wins ties. Both winner and loser deduct their dial power from their power track, and every played card is discarded face-up; card values do not cost additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3: secret simultaneous dials capped at min(7,current power); cards per participating character/mech; attacker abilities first; attacker wins ties; both pay dial power and discard played cards.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within its six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie waives popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after winning as aggressor, but not when driving off undefended workers without combat. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4: winner controls territory/resources and star; losing units retreat, leaving resources. Step 5: attacker popularity loss, defender none; loser draws a card if they revealed power on dial or through cards.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve an encounter only if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs and no additional mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses apply.
answers.evidence: Encounters: resolve after the whole Move action and all combats if character remains; on lost contested entry “the token stays”; gains go to “the encounter territory”; no normal action costs or mat/recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), looks at the available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. This applies to every player, not only the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Use the card as a fifth action section, with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule, except Rusviet can repeat. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement and stop restrictions still apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: “Every player's character” chooses on its first finish of a Move action there; at most one permanent card; Factory actions lack mat/recruit bonuses; bottom action moves one unit 2 spaces, or 3 with Speed for character/mech.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective, and you must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony may complete both starting objectives and keeps the second card after the first, so can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives: reveal only on your own turn before/after an action; meet all requirements at reveal; put both cards on deck bottom; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.

answers.answer: A star is earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's stars never block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all achievements; “A placed star is permanent”; “Other players' stars never block a goal”; sixth star “immediately ends play.”

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and the active player's ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; if the earlier player has ended the game, no later recruit star or bonus resolves. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to the territories they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence: bottom action primary benefit, coins and own recruit benefit before star; active then left then right; no later bonus after sixth star; pending battle movement is undone.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Five stars add $20. Four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories total (the Factory counts as three), adding $21. Thirteen resources make six pairs, adding $12. These sources add $53 to held coins, before the structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures; score only the selected tile. Tiebreakers are workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table at popularity 7–12 gives $4/$3/$2; Factory counts as three territories; example totals “$20 + $21 + $12 = $53”; structure bonus earned even if enemies control your structures' territories; listed tie order.
